summary: Follow-up bridgecall after the 2026-12-10 long-tail latency incidents. Reviewed root-cause hypotheses (cache eviction & bursty tails), validated fallback/rollback options, agreed on a concrete runbook and bench test schedule, and aligned on security/compliance checks for audit log retention and KMS key rotation. Decided to run a canary that adjusts prefix caching and short-sequence batching and then evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs.
topics: Root cause hypotheses: KV cache eviction, batching regressions, kernel mismatch
Rollback playbook and safe canary strategy
Telemetry and observability gaps (sample rates, spans)
Security/Compliance: audit logs, KMS, data residency concerns
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-14 14:00 UTC — Duration 72m. Attendees: Caroline, Marcus, Priya, Jun (Redwood); Alicia, Tommy, Lara, Ben, Marta (Veridian).

[00:00] Caroline Diaz: Okay hi everyone, thanks for jumping on. The goal today is a tight handoff on the rollback and resilience playbook then agree bench tests. we have about an hour plus so i'll try to keep us in scope.

[00:18] Alicia Gomez: Thanks Caroline. quick context — since the 12-10 event our execs want explicit rollback SLAs and proof we can avoid repeated long-tail latency. We also have compliance asking for retention of audit trails, so two tracks here.

[00:34] Marcus Lee: Hi, Marcus from Redwood SE. i'll go over the technical RCA we did and then we'll walk the runbook. note: some of the terminology in the internal report was mangled, the KV cache notes sometimes read as K V cache eviction which is the same thing.

[00:50] Tommy Wu: yea and just to be clear, we hit a tail where a small percentage of requests spiked to 1.2s from 120ms at peak. Mostly 8–12 token completions, so typical micro-interactions, which is odd.

[01:10] Jun Park: crosstalk — i want to add that the sequence length distribution shifted right for a subset of traffic during that window, there was also a GC pause on the customer side but that didn't line up exactly.

[01:32] Marcus Lee: Right, our working hypothesis is threefold: 1) KV cache eviction thrash when prefix keys expired during a burst 2) batching policy fallback created jitter for short sequences 3) an occasional kernel path mismatch on a small subset of instances (we saw one model variant serve a different optimized kernel after a hot restart). any of those could produce long tails.

[02:05] Ben Collins: That kernel mismatch, is that something redwood has seen before or is it an artifact of our private deployment?

[02:14] Marcus Lee: we've seen it in both private and hosted but more likely when autoscaling bounces nodes and the instance picks an older kernel binary. It's rare — like 0.1% of requests — but when combined with cache misses it's amplified.

[02:30] Lara Ibrahim: Security question — during rollbacks will we preserve audit logs and not lose telemetry? we need chain-of-custody for any mitigation steps.

[02:42] Priya Nair: good call. the playbook includes a step to snapshot traces and ship them to the customer's S3 (or their internal object store) prior to any rollback. we'll include exact retention TTLs and the sequence so it meets Veridian's compliance team needs.

[03:05] Marta Ruiz: And KMS — are keys rotated or disabled during a rollback? we cannot have keys unaccounted for.

[03:12] Jun Park: we recommend creating a temporary CMK alias for the canary, then rotate back or retire alias after the test. we never remove existing master keys — we just create a scoped alias for the canary tokens.

[03:34] Alicia Gomez: ok that helps. can you talk through the rollback playbook steps? the executive wants clear thresholds and owners.

[03:44] Caroline Diaz: sure — high level the playbook has three escalation levels:
- Level 1: Auto-fallback to a warm model variant with broader batching and disabled prefix caching (automated, no human in loop) if p99 latency > 500ms for 5 minutes.
- Level 2: Canary rollback to previous model binary + reconnect KV cache snapshot (manual with SE support) if p99 > 800ms or error rate rises 0.5% above baseline for 10 minutes.
- Level 3: Full rollback of the pool to the previous stable release and reduced QPS (SE and customer ops jointly run) if p99 > 1s and business impact high.

[04:35] Tommy Wu: question: that first bullet — auto-fallback to a variant with disabled prefix caching — won't disabling caching spike our token cost?

[04:45] Marcus Lee: yes it will increase cost a bit, but it's targeted and temporary. we also prefer disabling caching only for the small subset of affected routes, not whole tenant. we can scope by route tag in the console.

[05:00] Alicia Gomez: how deterministic is the auto-fallback? we saw some flapping during the incident.

[05:07] Marcus Lee: good point. the current hysteresis is 2 cycles of the measured window plus exponential backoff on retries. we can tighten that to avoid flapping — increase sample window to 90s and require two consecutive windows.

[05:28] Ben Collins: About telemetry, we noticed gaps — some spans were sampled out during the peak. can you run with higher sampling for the canary so we have full fidelity?

[05:38] Priya Nair: absolutely. we'll recommend 100% sampling for the canary traffic and a higher log retention for 72 hours. Caroline will add that to the doc.

[05:50] Alicia Gomez: Great. Let's talk acceptance criteria for bench tests. we want a clear pass/fail.

[06:00] Marcus Lee: Proposed bench test plan: replay the customer's obfuscated traces at 1.2x and 1.5x QPS, with the following checks: p50, p95, p99 latency thresholds (p99 < 300ms at 1.2x), KV cache hit ratio above 87%, and no kernel mismatch errors. We'll run three iterations each day until passing.

[06:25] Tommy Wu: can the bench run in our VPC or does it need Redwood infra? privacy constraints prefer in-VPC testing.

[06:33] Jun Park: we can run the bench in your VPC for Private deployments; for Hosted we provide a sandbox with obfuscated traces. we'll use transient test instances and not persist customer data.

[06:50] Lara Ibrahim: For audit purposes we need a signed artifact that lists exactly what changes were applied and when, plus who approved them. can redwood provide that?

[06:59] Caroline Diaz: yes we have a change artifact template we can fill out, sign with the SE and the customer's approver, and store with the audit logs. I'll attach the template in the shared folder.

[07:10] Ben Collins: we also want a post-test regression check to ensure quality didn't degrade — like a couple of eval prompts.

[07:18] Marcus Lee: understood. we'll include a small automated eval harness with prompts and scoring thresholds; if the score drops below the guardrail we'll abort the rollout.

[07:28] Alicia Gomez: timeline — what are we realistically looking at?

[07:34] Caroline Diaz: immediate next week: Marcus will prepare repro and a config diff for the canary. By 2026-12-17 we'll share the rollback document and the signed change artifact template. Bench testing week of 12/21, then a 48-hour observation. If all good, supervised gradual rollout after 12/28.

[07:55] Marta Ruiz: one more compliance item — retention period for traces must be at least 90 days for our audit team. is that doable?

[08:04] Priya Nair: by default we suggested 72 hours for high-res traces due to cost, but we can do a 90-day cold archive for obfuscated traces. need to confirm S3 lifecycle and access controls; i'll loop in support.

[08:20] Tommy Wu: i'd like to flag also we saw some anomalies around concurrent KV expirations during heavy bursts. is there a code-level mitigation or just config tuning?

[08:31] Marcus Lee: near term it's configuration: staggered TTLs, adaptive eviction thresholds, and small increases to cache capacity for the hot prefix set. longer term there is a runtime fix we can deliver that improves eviction grace period — that will need a micro release and goes through full QA.

[08:58] Jun Park: note: the runtime fix would eliminate about 80% of the observed eviction thrash in our sims but it requires a kernel bump which ties back to the kernel mismatch problem — so we'll coordinate kernel pinning in the canary.

[09:15] Ben Collins: How about cost — if we bump cache size that's additional monthly cost; we'll need an estimate.

[09:22] Marcus Lee: we'll include a delta estimate in the document. worst case small fraction of your infra spend for a transient month; we'll quantify.

[09:34] Alicia Gomez: ok recap and owners?

[09:38] Caroline Diaz: Recap: 1) Marcus to prep repro + config diff (due 12/20) 2) Caroline to share rollback playbook + change artifact template (due 12/17) 3) Tommy to share obfuscated traces (due 12/16) 4) Priya to confirm audit log retention approach and S3 policy (due 12/18) 5) Jun to scope runtime remediation ETA (due 12/23). We'll run bench tests week of 12/21 with 100% sampling and the eval harness.

[10:05] Alicia Gomez: sounds good. also please label every doc with the incident id: VER-2026-1210 so our compliance team can track it.

[10:12] Caroline Diaz: will do. we'll also attach the bench results and the signed artifact after the canary.

[10:22] Marta Ruiz: thanks everyone, this helps restore confidence.

[10:27] Tommy Wu: quick note — can we have a 30-min follow-up after the first bench run?

[10:31] Caroline Diaz: yes let's schedule a 30-min check-in for 2026-12-22. I'll ping calendar.

[10:38] Ben Collins: thanks, bye.

[10:40] End of call. Shared artifacts: rollback-playbook-draft (link: https://redwood.app/links/VER-2026-1210-playbook), change-artifact-template (link: https://redwood.app/links/change-artifact-template), bench-test-spec (link: https://redwood.app/links/bench-spec).

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and some technical terms transcribed as split tokens (e.g., KV -> K V). Natural speech, filler words, and minor overlaps present.
